title: Deterministic Linear-Time Minimum Spanning Tree Problem
statement:
Determine whether there exists a uniform deterministic comparison-based algorithm that, for every connected undirected graph with n vertices and m edges carrying distinct real-valued weights, computes a minimum spanning tree in worst-case O(m) time on a pointer machine, with edge weights accessed only by binary comparisons, in the model of Pettie and Ramachandran (2002).

Source: [Seth Pettie, Vijaya Ramachandran, "An Optimal Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithm," Journal of the ACM 49(1):16-34, 2002.](https://web.eecs.umich.edu/~pettie/papers/jacm-optmsf.pdf).

Status Open Status review date not recorded in this edition

Listed by [ProofAtlas](https://www.proofatlas.ai/open-problems/#problem-deterministic-linear-time-minimum-spanning-tree-problem). Status qualification is attributed to ProofAtlas; no full resolution is certified here.
source_name: ProofAtlas open problems; Seth Pettie, Vijaya Ramachandran, "An Optimal Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithm," Journal of the ACM 49(1):16-34, 2002.

title: Tree-polynomial ordering conjecture for non-crossing pairings
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tr}$ denote the relevant set of trees, let $p_{T,\sigma}$ be the tree polynomial associated with a tree $T$ and permutation $\sigma$, and let $p_{T,1}$ denote the polynomial for the identity permutation. Suppose

$$
0\leq n'_1\leq\cdots\leq n'_r.
$$

**Tree-polynomial ordering conjecture.** For every permutation $\sigma\in S_r$, there exists a re-ordering $\tau:\operatorname{Tr}\to\operatorname{Tr}$ such that $p_{T,\sigma}$ and $p_{\tau(T),1}$ are comparable and

$$
p_{T,\sigma}(n'_1,\ldots,n'_r)\leq p_{\tau(T),\operatorname{id}}(n'_1,\ldots,n'_r).
$$

Here, comparability means that one polynomial can be obtained as bounded above by the other through the inequality rules for the factors $[n_i]^k$. The paper presents this as a refinement suggested by numerical evidence, rather than as the theorem used to prove the preceding maximum statement.
source_name: Todd Kemp, Karl Mahlburg, Amarpreet Rattan and Clifford Smyth, “Enumeration of non-crossing pairings on bit strings”, arXiv:0906.2183 (2009).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.2183

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2009).

title: The local-volatility minimum conjecture for options on realized variance
statement:
Let $S$ follow a continuous stochastic-volatility model and let $V_T=\langle\log S\rangle_T$ be its realized variance. Let $\tilde S$ be the corresponding local-volatility model calibrated to the same volatility surface, with $\tilde V_T=\langle\log\tilde S\rangle_T$. For an integrable payoff function $f$ of realized variance, **Local-volatility minimum conjecture.** For every convex function $f$, one should have

$$
E\left[f(\tilde V_T)\right]\leq E\left[f(V_T)\right].
$$

This conjecture says that the calibrated local-volatility model gives the minimum possible value of a convex option on realized variance, while the variance swap itself has the same value in both models because $E[\tilde V_T]=E[V_T]$. The paper's abstract states that it provides a counterexample to this widespread conjecture, so the conjecture is refuted.
source_name: Mathias Beiglboeck, Peter Friz and Stephan Sturm, “Is the minimum value of an option on variance generated by local volatility?”, arXiv:1001.4031 (2011).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.4031

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2010); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Optimal precoding matrices conjecture for slow-fading MIMO channels
statement:
Let $\Gamma(\mathbf{Q},R)$ denote the goodput-to-power ratio, let $P_{\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{Q},R)$ denote the outage probability, and let $\overline{P}$ be the available transmit-power constraint. Let $n_t$ be the number of transmit antennas and let $\mathbf{I}_{n_t}$ be the $n_t\times n_t$ identity matrix. **Optimal precoding matrices conjecture.** There exists a power threshold $\overline{P}_0$ such that:

- if $\overline{P}\leq\overline{P}_0$, then

$$
\mathbf{Q}^*\in\arg\min_{\mathbf{Q}}P_{\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{Q},R)\quad\Rightarrow\quad\mathbf{Q}^*\in\arg\max_{\mathbf{Q}}\Gamma(\mathbf{Q},R);
$$

- if $\overline{P}>\overline{P}_0$, then $\Gamma(\mathbf{Q},R)$ has a unique maximum at

$$
\mathbf{Q}^*=\frac{p^*}{n_t}\mathbf{I}_{n_t},\qquad p^*\leq\overline{P}.
$$

The conjecture has been validated for all the special cases solved in the paper. It says that below the threshold, maximizing the goodput-to-power ratio is equivalent to minimizing outage probability, whereas above the threshold uniform power allocation is optimal and using all available power is generally suboptimal for energy efficiency.
source_name: E. V. Belmega and S. Lasaulce, “Energy-Efficient Precoding for Multiple-Antenna Terminals”, arXiv:1011.4597 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4597

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

title: The product-dimension conjecture for forbidden submatrices
statement:
Let $F$ be a fixed $(0,1)$-matrix. For matrices $M$ and $N$, write $[M\,|\,N]$ for their horizontal concatenation and let $k\cdot M$ denote the concatenation of $k$ copies of $M$. Let $I_k$ be the $k\times k$ identity matrix, let $I_k^c$ be its $(0,1)$-complement, and let $T_k$ be the upper-triangular $(0,1)$-matrix. For matrices $X$ and $Y$, let $X\times Y$ be their product whose columns consist of every possible concatenation of a column of $X$ and a column of $Y$, and extend this definition to $p$ factors. Define $X(F)$ to be the smallest $p$ such that $F\prec A_1\times A_2\times\cdots\times A_p$ for every choice of each $A_i$ among $I_{m/p}$, $I_{m/p}^c$, and $T_{m/p}$. Here $F\prec A$ means that $F$ is a configuration of $A$, and ${\text{forb}}(m,F)$ is the maximum number of columns in an $m$-rowed simple matrix avoiding $F$. **Product-dimension conjecture.** For every fixed matrix $F$,

$$
{\text{forb}}(m,F)=\Theta\left(m^{X(F)-1}\right).
$$

The preceding product constructions give the lower bound ${\text{forb}}(m,F)=\Omega(m^{X(F)-1})$ under the stated divisibility assumptions. The conjecture asserts that this lower bound has the correct order of growth; the supplied text does not indicate whether it has been proved or disproved.
source_name: Richard P. Anstee and Linyuan Lu, “Repeated columns and an old chestnut”, arXiv:1305.0603 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0603

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

title: Anstee–Sali conjecture on forbidden configuration growth
statement:
Let $F$ be a $k\times \ell$ matrix with $F\ne \begin{bmatrix}0\\ 1\end{bmatrix}$. Let $I_k$ be the $k\times k$ identity matrix, $I_k^c$ its (0,1)-complement, and $T_k$ the $k\times k$ upper triangular matrix whose $i$th column has 1's in rows $1,2,\ldots,i$. For matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_p$, let $A_1\times\cdots\times A_p$ be their product configuration formed by stacking one column from each factor in every possible combination. Define $\operatorname*{forb}(m,F)$ as the maximum number of columns in an $m$-rowed simple matrix avoiding $F$. Let $X(F)$ be the largest $p$ for which there are choices $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_p\in\{I_{m/p},I^c_{m/p},T_{m/p}\}$ such that $F\nprec A_1\times A_2\times\cdots\times A_p$. **Anstee–Sali conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname*{forb}(m,F)=\Theta(m^{X(F)}).
$$

This conjecture predicts the precise polynomial order of the extremal function for every forbidden matrix other than the excluded two-row column. It is a central proposed framework for forbidden configuration problems, but the supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved in full.
source_name: Attila Sali and Sam Spiro, “Forbidden Families of Minimal Quadratic and Cubic Configurations”, arXiv:1703.05602 (2017).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1307.1148](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.1148), [arXiv:1210.8189](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8189).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.05602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

title: Born winner/silver spoon regime conjecture for the multiplicative coalescent
statement:
Let $(\boldsymbol{x}^{\scriptscriptstyle(n)})_{n\geqslant 1}$ satisfy Condition II$\tau$ for some $\tau\in(3,4)$, and let $M_n$ be as in the leader theorem. Write $\mathcal{W}_n$ for the event that the component containing $x_1^{\scriptscriptstyle(n)}$ is always the leader, meaning that the identity of the leader never changes. Assume $c_1>c_2$. **Born winner/silver spoon regime conjecture.** There exists $\delta>0$ such that

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(M_n^-\geqslant K)>\delta
$$

for every $K>0$. Moreover,

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}(\mathcal{W}_n)>0.
$$

The first assertion predicts that, under Condition II$\tau$, the negative part of the leader-stabilization time is not tight, complementing the tightness result for its positive part. The second asserts a positive limiting probability that the component containing the largest initial particle remains leader forever; both claims are left conjectural in the stated regime.
source_name: Louigi Addario-Berry, Shankar Bhamidi and Sanchayan Sen, “A probabilistic approach to the leader problem in random graphs”, arXiv:1703.09908 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.09908

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

title: Poisson distribution conjecture for the number of mmWave retransmissions
statement:
Let $N^*$ denote the random variable counting the number of transmissions required in the intermittent mmWave-link model, let $A$ be the model parameter, and let $R_{\min}$ and $\alpha$ be the corresponding minimum transmission rate and path-loss exponent. **Poisson distribution conjecture.** For every $N\in\mathbb{N}\smallsetminus\{0\}$,

$$
\mathcal{P}\{N^*=N\}=\frac{(\log_e A^2)^{N-1}}{(N-1)!A^2}.
$$

Equivalently, $N^*-1$ follows a Poisson distribution with parameter

$$
\log_e A^2=\frac{2R_{\min}}{\alpha\log_2 e},
$$

and consequently

$$
\mathbb{E}[N^*]=\operatorname*{Var}(N^*)=\frac{2R_{\min}}{\alpha\log_2 e}+1.
$$

The preceding integral expression is not easily reduced to closed form for $N\geq 3$, so this conjecture proposes an explicit distribution and corresponding moments for the transmission-count random variable. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been proved or refuted.
source_name: Nicola di Pietro, Mattia Merluzzi, Emilio Calvanese Strinati and Sergio Barbarossa, “Resilient Design of 5G Mobile-Edge Computing Over Intermittent mmWave Links”, arXiv:1901.01894 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01894

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

title: Sottile–Williams conjecture on simple Bruhat interval polytopes
statement: Let $v,w\in\mathfrak{S}_n$ with $v\leq w$, and let $Q_{v,w}$ be the Bruhat interval polytope whose vertices are the permutations $u\in[v,w]$. For each $u\in[v,w]$, let $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ be the transitive reduction of the acyclic graph associated with the vertex $u$; by the preceding proposition, $u$ is simple in $Q_{v,w}$ exactly when the underlying undirected graph of $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ is a forest. **Sottile–Williams conjecture.** The polytope $Q_{v,w}$ is simple if and only if the vertices $v$ and $w$ are simple. Equivalently, if the graphs $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_v$ and $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_v$ are forests, then $\widetilde{G}^{v,w}_u$ is a forest for every $v\leq u\leq w$. This generalizes Conjecture 7.16 of Le–Ma, which concerns the corresponding case with the lower endpoint equal to the identity permutation. The conjecture asserts that checking simplicity at the endpoints suffices to determine simplicity of the entire Bruhat interval polytope.
source_name: Eunjeong Lee, Mikiya Masuda and Seonjeong Park, “Toric Bruhat interval polytopes”, arXiv:1904.10187 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

title: Conjecture A on adjoining prescribed matrix blocks to division-ring embeddings
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n>1$, and let $\varphi:F\to M_n(G)$ be a ring embedding, where $G$ and $F$ are division rings. Suppose that $a$ and $b$ are positive integers satisfying

$$
a+b=n+1.
$$

Let $A$ be an $a\times b$ matrix with entries in $G$. **Conjecture A.** There exist division-ring extensions $G\subseteq G^\prime$ and $F\subseteq F^\prime$, together with a ring embedding $\varphi^\prime:F^\prime\to M_n(G^\prime)$ such that $\varphi^\prime|_F=\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Im}(\varphi^\prime)$ contains a matrix whose upper-right $a\times b$ block is $A$. The conjecture would provide the extensions needed to construct tight embeddings for arbitrary parameters, and its validity would consequently disprove the pure semisimplicity conjecture; the paper establishes only partial cases, including those yielding tight embeddings for $n<5$.
source_name: Jan Šaroch, “Pure semisimplicity conjecture and Artin problem for dimension sequences”, arXiv:1909.13864 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13864

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

title: Amended Gaussian optimality conjecture for the Han–Kobayashi region
statement: Let $(N_1,N_2,u,q_1,q_2)$ denote positive channel and power parameters, and let the **isotropic condition** mean that the maximum in the stated theorem is achieved by isotropic Gaussian inputs for every positive integer dimension. Let 1-letter HKGS without power control and 1-letter HKGS with power control denote the corresponding Gaussian Han–Kobayashi schemes. **Amended Gaussian optimality conjecture.** The set of $(N_1,N_2,u,q_1,q_2)$ satisfying the isotropic condition in the theorem equals the set of parameters for which 1-letter HKGS without power control matches 1-letter HKGS with power control. This conjecture isolates the stability regime in which power control is unnecessary for the Gaussian Han–Kobayashi bound. The paper states that the isotropic parameter set is nonempty and that a more precise characterization remains open; its status evidence says that disproving this conjecture would disprove optimality of HKGS with power control for the whole capacity region.
source_name: Jingbo Liu, “Stability of the Gaussian Stationary Point in the Han-Kobayashi Region for Z-Interference Channels”, arXiv:2209.00163 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00163

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2022).

title: Coefficient-of-asymmetry reformulation of the Lonely Runner Conjecture
statement:
Let $\mathbf{n}\in\mathbb{Z}^d_{>0}$ be a velocity vector, meaning that its entries are distinct and relatively prime, and let

$$
Z(\mathbf{n})=\mathbb{R}\mathbf{n}+[0,1]^d.
$$

An interior lattice point is a point $\mathbf{w}\in\operatorname{int}(Z(\mathbf{n}))\cap\mathbb{Z}^d$, and $\operatorname{ca}(Z(\mathbf{n}),\mathbf{w})$ denotes its coefficient of asymmetry. **Coefficient-of-asymmetry reformulation.** For every velocity vector $\mathbf{n}\in\mathbb{Z}^d_{>0}$, there exists an interior lattice point $\mathbf{w}\in\operatorname{int}(Z(\mathbf{n}))\cap\mathbb{Z}^d$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ca}(Z(\mathbf{n}),\mathbf{w})\leq d.
$$

This is presented as an equivalent geometric formulation of the Lonely Runner Conjecture, via the identity between the minimum coefficient of asymmetry and the gap of loneliness. Its status is therefore the same as that conjecture and remains open in general.
source_name: Matthias Beck and Matthias Schymura, “Deep lattice points in zonotopes, lonely runners, and lonely rabbits”, arXiv:2301.12182 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12182

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

title: Conjecture on extremal subgroup counts for ${\rm PSL}_2(p)$
statement:
For a finite group $G$, let $i(G)$ be the number of isomorphism classes of non-identity proper subgroups of $G$, let $c(G)$ be the number of conjugacy classes of such subgroups, let $s(G)$ be the number of conjugacy classes of such self-normalising subgroups, and let $n(G)$ be the number of conjugacy classes of such non-self-normalising subgroups. A subgroup $H\leq G$ is self-normalising when $H=N_G(H)$. Let $G={\rm PSL}_2(p)$ for a prime $p$. **Extremal subgroup-count conjecture.** There is an infinite set of primes $p$ for which $G={\rm PSL}_2(p)$ satisfies

$$
i(G)=17,\qquad c(G)=18,\qquad s(G)=6,\qquad n(G)=12.
$$

Theorem-level lower bounds show that these are the minimum values under consideration for all sufficiently large primes, and computational evidence has found more than $1.2\times 10^6$ primes attaining all four bounds. The conjecture asserts that this phenomenon occurs for infinitely many primes.
source_name: Gareth A. Jones, “Counting conjugacy classes of subgroups of PSL_2(p)”, arXiv:2411.02219 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.02219

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

title: Two-cluster convergence conjecture for causal transformer dynamics with simple dominant eigendirection
statement:
Let $Q$ and $K$ be arbitrary matrices, and let $V$ be diagonalizable with $d$ different positive real eigenvalues. Denote its largest eigenvalue by $\lambda_{\max}$, and let $\xi$ be a unit eigenvector satisfying

$$
V\xi=\lambda_{\max}\xi.
$$

For the causal transformer dynamics, **two-cluster convergence conjecture.** For almost every starting point $(x_1(0),\ldots,x_n(0))$ with respect to the volume measure on $(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n$,

$$
\forall k\in[n],\qquad \lim_{t\to\infty}x_k(t)\in\\{\xi,-\xi\\}.
$$

This conjectures that, when the dominant eigenvalue is positive and has a one-dimensional eigendirection under the stated diagonalizability assumptions, causal attention generically drives all tokens into two antipodal clusters. The claim is presented as part of the paper's conjectural extension beyond the proved identity-matrix case; its resolution is not supplied here.
source_name: Nikita Karagodin, Yury Polyanskiy and Philippe Rigollet, “Clustering in Causal Attention Masking”, arXiv:2411.04990 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04990

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “While a rigorous proof of this dimension-reduction remains an open problem for future investigation, this phenomenon motivates our focus on low-dimensional cases (specifically $d=2$) throughout this section.”

title: Robins' conjecture on Fourier transforms of convex centrally symmetric bodies
statement:
Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be convex, centrally symmetric bodies. Suppose that $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ are not multi-tilers, meaning that neither set $k$-tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a translation set for any positive integer $k$. Their Fourier transforms are defined by

$$
\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{P}}(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}1_{\mathcal{P}}(x)e^{-2\pi i\langle x,\xi\rangle}\,dx,
$$

and similarly for $\mathcal{Q}$, where $1_{\mathcal{P}}$ and $1_{\mathcal{Q}}$ are the characteristic functions.

**Robins' conjecture.** If

$$
\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{P}}(\xi)=\widehat{1}_{\mathcal{Q}}(\xi)
$$

for every $\xi\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, then $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ coincide up to rigid motions, except on a set of measure zero; equivalently, the two conditions hold if and only if the bodies coincide up to such motions.

The conjecture concerns whether lattice samples of the Fourier transform determine a non-multi-tiling convex centrally symmetric body up to rigid motion. The paper states that it constructs a counterexample, so the conjecture is refuted in the dimension covered by that construction; the supplied excerpt does not specify the dimension or the precise counterexample.
source_name: Oleg Asipchuk, “Note on Robins' Conjecture in Dimension Four and Higher”, arXiv:2509.26587 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26587

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2025); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Crofton-type conjecture for random Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
statement:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a centered, time-symmetric, exhaustive or periodically exhaustive law-defining datum. Let $L\subset M$ be a closed Lagrangian submanifold. The datum specifies an almost complex structure $J$ and the associated Riemannian metric $g$.

**Crofton-type conjecture.** There exist a constant $C>0$ and a smooth function $\rho:M\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, depending only on $\mathcal{D}$ and $L$ and satisfying

$$
\int_M \rho\,\omega^n=\operatorname{vol}(M),
$$

such that, for every closed Lagrangian submanifold $K\subset M$,

$$
\int_{\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)} \#(L\cap\varphi(K))\,d\mu_{\operatorname{Ham}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\varphi)=C\cdot\operatorname{vol}_{\rho\cdot g}(K).
$$

In particular, there exist constants $C',C”>0$ such that

$$
C'\cdot\operatorname{vol}_g(K)\leq\int_{\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)}\#(L\cap\varphi(K))\,d\mu_{\operatorname{Ham}}^{\mathcal{D}}(\varphi)\leq C”\cdot\operatorname{vol}_g(K).
$$

The conjecture seeks a Crofton formula for expected Lagrangian intersection counts, with a density-rescaled metric accounting for the nonuniform behavior seen in simulations. The supplied text gives numerical evidence and explains why the standard metric does not yield an exact formula, but states no resolution; the conjecture remains open.
source_name: Adrian Dawid, “Random Hamiltonians I: Probability measures and random walks on the Hamiltonian diffeomorphism group”, arXiv:2510.03190 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).

title: Matching conjecture for the stochastic Bessel limiting point process
statement:
For $a\geq 0$, let $\mathcal{M}_a=\sum_{i\geq 1}\delta_{\mu_a^{\infty}(i)}$ be the limiting point process, and let $(g_j)_{j\geq 1}$ be independent exponential random variables with parameters $j(j+a)/2$. Define

$$
\hat{\mu}_a^{\infty}(k):=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}g_j,\qquad k\geq 1.
$$

**Matching conjecture.** For all $a\geq 0$, the joint distributions of $(\hat{\mu}_a^{\infty}(i),\;i\geq 1)$ and $(\mu_a^{\infty}(i),\;i\geq 1)$ are equal. As a corollary, using the explicit expression for the density of $\hat{\mu}_a^{\infty}(1)$,

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{j-1}\frac{j(2j+a)}{2}\binom{j+a}{j}e^{-\frac{j(j+a)}{2}x},
$$

this matching yields

$$
\mathbb{P}\big(\exists t\geq 0,\;R^{-a}(t)\geq\mu+bt\big)=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{j-1}\left[\binom{j+a/b}{j}+\binom{j+a/b-1}{j-1}\right]e^{-2\mu j(jb+a)},
$$

where $R^{-a}$ is a reflected Brownian motion with drift $-a$.

The conjecture extends the proved equality of the largest points at $a=0$ to the entire point process and all $a\geq 0$. If true, it would provide an unexpected diffusion representation of the exponential-gap construction and an exact formula for the hitting probability of a reflected Brownian motion with negative drift.
source_name: Laure Dumaz and Hugo Magaldi, “The spectrum of the stochastic Bessel operator at high temperature”, arXiv:2603.27602 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

title: Finite area determination conjecture for Kähler–Einstein metrics on a product of surfaces
statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be the closed surface under consideration, let $\mathcal L^*(g)$ denote the relevant set of surface subgroups of genus $g$, and let $A(h)(\Pi)$ be the associated area function of a metric $h$ on $\Sigma\times\Sigma$. **Finite area determination conjecture.** There is a finite set $\mathcal L_0\subset\mathcal L^*(g)$ such that, if $h$ and $\hat h$ are Kähler–Einstein metrics on $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ satisfying

$$
A(h)(\Pi)=A(\hat h)(\Pi)\quad\text{for all }\Pi\in\mathcal L_0,
$$

then $h$ and $\hat h$ are isometric, and the isometry is homotopic to the identity. This asks whether finitely many minimal-Lagrangian area measurements determine a Kähler–Einstein metric up to an isometry homotopic to the identity; the supplied text presents it as a new question, with no resolution stated.
source_name: Ben Lowe, Fernando C. Marques and André Neves, “Counting Minimal Lagrangians Via Mirzakhani Functions”, arXiv:2605.04614 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04614

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

title: Stanley's distinct-roots conjecture for dimer-covering denominators
statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $A_{k,n}$ denote the number of domino tilings of a $k\times n$ rectangle, and let

$$
F_k(x)=\sum_{n\geq 0}A_{k,n}x^n.
$$

Stanley's denominator $Q_k(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ is defined by $F_k(x)=P_k(x)/Q_k(x)$ and $Q_k(0)=1$; explicitly, with $\ell=\left\lfloor k/2\right\rfloor$, set

$$
c_j=\cos\frac{j\pi}{k+1}+\sqrt{1+\cos^2\frac{j\pi}{k+1}},\qquad \bar{c}_j=\cos\frac{j\pi}{k+1}-\sqrt{1+\cos^2\frac{j\pi}{k+1}},
$$

and, for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,\ell\}$,

$$
a_S=\left(\prod_{j\in S}c_j\right)\left(\prod_{j\in\{1,\ldots,\ell\}\setminus S}\bar{c}_j\right).
$$

Then

$$
Q_k(x)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\prod_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,\ell\}}(1-a_Sx),&k\text{ even},\\[1.2em]
\displaystyle\prod_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,\ell\}}(1-a_S^2x^2),&k\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Stanley's conjecture.** The polynomial $Q_k(x)$ has distinct roots.
This conjecture concerns the simplicity of the poles of the dimer-covering generating functions. It is refuted: the paper proves that $Q_{14h-1}(x)$ and $Q_{30h-1}(x)$ have repeated roots for every $h\geq1$, with $k=13$ the smallest counterexample.
source_name: Xuejun Guo and Zhengyu Tao, “Counterexamples to Stanley's conjecture on dimer coverings”, arXiv:2605.28195 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28195

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Let $Q_k(x)$ be Stanley's explicit denominator for the dimer-covering generating function $F_k(x)=\sum_{n\ge0}A_{k,n}x^n$ of $k\times n$ rectangles.”

title: Pemantle's conjecture that CNC implies CNA
statement:
Let $cmu
a$ be a probability measure on $c{0,1}^n$. It is **CNC** if every pair of disjoint increasing events is negatively correlated, and it is **CNA** if every pair of disjoint subsets of coordinates has negatively associated restrictions under conditioning on any increasing function of the remaining coordinates. In the setting of generalized urn measures, write $R^+$ for the property that every external field transformation $W\circ\mu$, with $W_i\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ for all $i$, is negatively correlated.

**Pemantle's conjecture.** CNC implies CNA. In particular, the equivalent formulation considered here is that $R^+$ implies CNA.

The conjecture asks whether the stronger conditional negative association property follows from conditional negative correlation. The paper notes that a negative answer for generalized urn measures would provide a counterexample to the CNC-implies-CNA conjecture, and that CNC for this class is equivalent to the stated $R^+$ property; its resolution is not supplied here.
source_name: Jeff Kahn and Michael Neiman, “Conditional negative association for competing urns”, arXiv:1001.0610 (2010).

title: Faudree–Schelp–Gyárfás–Tuza conjecture on strong edge-coloring of subcubic graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $Delta(G)=3$.

**Faudree–Schelp–Gyárfás–Tuza conjecture.** The following bounds hold:

1. $chi'_s(G)\le 10$.
2. If $G$ is bipartite, then $chi'_s(G)\le 9$.
3. If $G$ is planar, then $chi'_s(G)\le 9$.
4. If $G$ is bipartite and for each edge $xy\in E(G)$ one has $d(x)+d(y)\le 5$, then $chi'_s(G)\le 6$.
5. If $G$ is bipartite and has no 4-cycle, then $chi'_s(G)\le 7$.
6. If $G$ is bipartite and its girth is large, then $chi'_s(G)\le 5$.

The conjecture concerns strong edge-colorings, in which edges at distance at most 1 receive distinct colors; equivalently, it concerns proper vertex-colorings of the square of the line graph. The source states that four parts have been confirmed, while the counterexample presented in the paper resolves the remaining conjectural claims.
source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, “Strong Edge-Coloring of Cubic Bipartite Graphs: A Counterexample”, arXiv:2112.01443 (2022).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1412.8358](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.8358).

title: A stronger form of Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
statement:
Show that there exists $C>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and for all $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to \mathbb{R}$ we have
	

$$
\text{Var}(f)\le \|f\|_\infty\deg(f)^C \max_{1\le j\le n}\|D_j f\|_2.
$$
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing

title: Heat-smoothing conjecture
statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$ and $1< p < \infty$. Show that there exists $c_p>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to \mathbb{R}$ of the form $f=\sum_{|S|\ge d}\widehat{f}(S)\chi_S$, we have 
	

$$
\|P_t f\|_p\le e^{-tdc_p}\|f\|_p, \qquad t\ge 0,
$$

 where $P_t=e^{-t\Delta}$ is the heat semigroup on $\{-1,1\}^n$.
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing

title: Heat-smoothing: a weaker form
statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$ and $1< p < \infty$. Show that there exists $c_p>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to \mathbb{R}$ of the form $f=\sum_{|S|\ge d}\widehat{f}(S)\chi_S$, we have 
	

$$
\|\Delta f\|_p\ge dc_p\|f\|_p,
$$

	where $\Delta$ is the generator of the heat semigroup $P_t=e^{-t\Delta}$.
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing (posed by Paata Ivanisvili)

title: Gaussian heat-smoothing
statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$ and $1< p < \infty$. Show that there exists $c_p>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all polynomials $f\in \text{Lin}\{x^k,k\ge d\}$, we have
	

$$
\|P_t f\|_p\le e^{-tdc_p}\|f\|_p, \qquad t\ge 0,
$$

	where $P_t=e^{-tN}$ is the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup on the Gaussian space.
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing

title: Gaussian heat-smoothing: a weaker form
statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$ and $1< p < \infty$. Show that there exists $c_p>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all polynomials $f\in \text{Lin}\{x^k,k\ge d\}$, we have
	

$$
\|Nf\|_p\ge dc_p\|f\|_p,
$$

	where $N=\Delta-x\nabla$ is the generator of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup.
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing (posed by Paata Ivanisvili)

title: Best constants in Bohnenblust-Hille inequalities for hypercubes
statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$. Show that there exists $C>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all polynomials $f=\sum_{|S|\le d}\widehat{f}(S)\chi_S$ on $\{-1,1\}^n$ of degree at most $d$, we have 
	

$$
\left(\sum_{|S|\le d}|\widehat{f}(S)|^{\frac{2d}{d+1}}\right)^{\frac{d+1}{2d}}\le d^C \|f\|_{\infty}.
$$
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing

title: Homogeneous case
statement:
Fix $d\ge 1$. Show that there exists $C>0$ such that for all $n\ge 1$ and all $d$-homogeneous polynomials $f=\sum_{|S|= d}\widehat{f}(S)\chi_S$ on $\{-1,1\}^n$, we have 
	

$$
\left(\sum_{|S|= d}|\widehat{f}(S)|^{\frac{2d}{d+1}}\right)^{\frac{d+1}{2d}}\le d^C \|f\|_{\infty}.
$$
source_name: AimPL: Analysis on the hypercube with applications to quantum computing

title: Pathological sets (problem 4)
statement: Does the existence of a set $E$ such that $E$ is not $\sigma$-finite in dimension $1$ but for every superlinear gauge function $\varphi$, $H_\varphi(E) = 0$ imply that there is a counterexample to the Borel conjecture?

title: Log-Brunn-Minkowski Inequality
statement:
Show that if $K$ and $L$ symmetric convex bodies in ${\\mathbb{R}}^n$, then for all $0 \leq t \leq 1$ the following hods

$$
|tK +_\circ (1-t)L| \geq |K|^t |L|^{1-t}
$$

with equality if and only if $K = L$ or $K$ and $L$ are parallelograms with parallel sides.
source_name: AimPL: Symmetry and convexity in geometric inequalities

title: $L_p$-Brunn Minkowski inequality
statement:
Show that if $K$ and $L$ symmetric convex bodies in ${\\mathbb{R}}^n$, then for all $0 \leq t \leq 1$ and $p\geq 0$ 

$$
|tK +_p (1-t)L| \geq |K|^t |L|^{1-t}.
$$
source_name: AimPL: Symmetry and convexity in geometric inequalities

title: Cycle + Erdos-Renyi
statement:
Prove that for $p=\frac \epsilon n$, $\epsilon>0$ fixed, the nonreversible chain has $t_{\text{mix}}\asymp \log n$.

Prove that when $p=\epsilon n^{-\frac 32}$ the nonreversible chain has $t_{\text{mix}}=\tilde O(\sqrt n)$.
source_name: AimPL: Markov chain mixing times (posed by Balazs Gerencser)

title: Some Questions — Question 13
statement: For a graph sequence $(G_n)$ define $e((G_n))=\liminf |E(G_n)|/|V(G_n)|$, and define its combinatorial cost as the infimum of $e((H_n))$ over graph sequences $(H_n)$ on the same vertex sets for which the identity maps have uniformly bounded bi-Lipschitz constants. If $(G_n)$ and $(H_n)$ converge locally to the same limit, must they have the same combinatorial cost?
source_name: Abert - Some questions (pdf) (2010)

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.28
statement: Suppose that $P$ is a non-linear polynomial with real coefficients. Show that $P^2(z)+P'(z)$ has non-real zeros. We conjecture that the lower bound for the number of non-real zeros is $\deg(P)-1$. If $P$ itself has only real zeros, this is proved by P\'olya and Szeg\"o . For the origin of this problem, see Problem 2.64. (S. Hellerstein)
source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.56
statement: Let $S_R(q)$ be the class of normalised univalent functions in $\mathbb{D}$ with real coefficients that admit a quasi-conformal extension to the whole plane with complex dilatation bounded (in modulus) almost everywhere by $q$, $q < 1$. Following the notation in Problem 6.44, prove (or disprove) that, if $f\in S_R(p)$ and $g\in S_R(q)$, then $f\otimes g\in S_R(r)$. (J. G. Krzyz)
source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.39
statement: (Subadditivity problem for analytic capacity) Prove or disprove the existence of a constant $M$ such that \[\gamma(K_1\cup K_2)\leq M\{\gamma(K_1)+\gamma(K_2)\}\] for all compact sets $K_1, K_2$ in $\mathbb{C}$. Even the case where $\gamma(K_2)=0$ is open. For background, see Garnett . (J. Korevaar)
source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.76
statement: Prove or disprove the following statement: If $K$ is a compact subset of $\mathbb{C}$ with continuous analytic capacity $\alpha(K)= 0$, then \[\alpha(E\setminus K)=\alpha(E)\] for all compact subsets $E$ of $\mathbb{C}$. An interesting special case is when $K$ is a $C^1$-arc. The case when $K$ is a $C^{1+\varepsilon}$-arc has already been settled. (A. G. O'Farrell)
source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — Matrix version of 6 deviations suffice
statement: Prove or disprove: there exists a universal constant $C$ such that, for any choice of $n$ symmetric matrices $H_1,\dots,H_n\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ satisfying $\|H_k\|\leq 1$ (for all $k=1,\dots,n$ ), there exists $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n \in \{ \pm1\}$ such that $\left\| \sum_{k=1}^n \varepsilon_k H_k \right\| \leq C \sqrt{n}.$

title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — Feige's conjecture
statement: Prove or disprove the following conjecture by Feige : Given $n$ independent random variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ s.t., for all $i$ , $X_i \geq 0$ and $\mathbb{E} X_i = 1$ we have $\mathrm{Prob}\left( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i \geq n+1 \right) \leq 1 - e^{-1}$ .

title: Multiple ergodic averages — Problem 17
statement: Suppose that the polynomials $p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\in \mathbb Z[t]$ are rationally independent and have zero constant term. Show that for every $A\in \mathcal X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $n\in \mathbb N$ such that $$ \mu(A\cap T_1^{p_1(n)}A\cap \cdots\cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)}A)\geq \mu(A)^{\ell+1}-\varepsilon. $$

title: Uniform geometry in complex renormalization
statement: Let $f_i(z)=z^2+c_i$ range over finitely many critically periodic quadratic polynomials, let $g_n$ be the iterated tuning $f_1\vdash\cdots\vdash f_n$, and write $n_k=\prod_{i\le k}m_i$ for the products of critical periods. Prove that every set $\{g_n^{n_k\ell+i}(0):0\le\ell<m_{k+1}\}$ has geometry bounded uniformly for all $i\le n_k$, $k<n$, and $n$.
source_name: Stony Brook - Open Problems in Dynamical Systems (proposed by Mary Rees)

title: Exceptional parameters without D(n)-quadruples
statement: For each $n\in\{-3,3,5,8,12,20\}$, prove that no set of four distinct positive integers has property $D(n)$, meaning that every pairwise product plus $n$ is a square. (The page's original exceptional set also contained $-1$ and $-4$, which subsequent results on the same page settle.)

title: Associativity and Hamiltonian-product comparison for preorbifold cohomology
statement: **Theorem 6.** Let $Y$ be an almost complex manifold with a $T$-action preserving the almost complex structure. Then $(PH^{*,\diamond}_T(Y),\wedge)$ is a graded, associative ring. statement:

\[
n^{2/d+\varepsilon}\leq \mathbb{E}_n[\operatorname{Dist}(\gamma_n,0)^2]\leq n^{2-\varepsilon}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).
